## How it works

Access to AI Gateway crosses two trust boundaries. **Inbound**, your app authenticates to the gateway
endpoint. **Outbound**, the gateway authenticates to each model or tool with its own credential, which you
set up in [Call backends with managed identities](../12-backend-identity/README.md).

For inbound Entra access, the caller gets an access token for the audience `https://azure-api.net/aigateway`
and sends it in the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header. The gateway validates the token at its edge, then
checks the caller's Azure RBAC role assignments for the model alias or MCP server in the request. Without a
matching role, it answers `403` before any policy or backend runs. These roles grant **runtime** access only,
not gateway administration.

| Role | Role ID | Grants | Assignable at |
|---|---|---|---|
| AI Gateway User | `caad7a21-134e-43f4-a550-c5ffc17e051c` | List and invoke models, list and call MCP tools | Gateway, model alias, or MCP server |
| AI Gateway Models User | `a6b68e3d-a1f0-4c60-8678-237c050cf4ea` | List and invoke models | Gateway or model alias |
| AI Gateway Tools User | `dce03f8d-857f-4e40-a90d-67770fa6ecd2` | List and call tools within MCP servers | Gateway or MCP server |

| Caller | Token type | Scope to request |
|---|---|---|
| App that signs users in with MSAL | Delegated (on behalf of the user) | `https://azure-api.net/aigateway/Data.All` |
| Service principal, managed identity, or agent identity | App-only | `https://azure-api.net/aigateway/.default` |
| You, signed in to the Azure CLI | Delegated | `az account get-access-token --resource https://azure-api.net/aigateway` |

Policies that count by **Caller identity**, such as the token limits and budgets in labs 06 and 07, keep
working: for Entra callers, the gateway combines the token's tenant ID (`tid`) and object ID (`oid`), so each
principal gets its own counter.

## Grant a data-plane role

Grant yourself **AI Gateway Models User** on the whole gateway. Do this once, whichever track you follow to
call the gateway afterward. Role scopes are Azure resource IDs:

| Scope | Resource ID |
|---|---|
| Gateway | `/subscriptions/<subscription-id>/resourceGroups/<resource-group>/providers/Microsoft.ApiManagement/aigateways/<gateway>` |
| Model alias | `<gateway resource ID>/workspaces/default/aliases/<alias>` |
| MCP server | `<gateway resource ID>/workspaces/default/toolServers/<mcp-server-name>` |

<!-- track: portal | Portal -->

### Start a role assignment

Open the [AI Gateway portal](https://ai.gateway.azure.com), select your gateway, and select
**Access** › **Entra ID** › **Add role assignments**.

### Choose access

On **Choose access**, pick what the identities can use:

- **All models and tools in the gateway** grants **AI Gateway User** at the gateway.
- **All models in the gateway** grants **AI Gateway Models User** at the gateway.
- **All tools in the gateway** grants **AI Gateway Tools User** at the gateway.
- **Specific resources** lets you select model aliases and MCP servers under **Resources**, then choose one
  compatible **Role** for all of them.

Select **All models in the gateway**, then **Next**.

![The Add role assignments wizard on the Choose access step](../assets/screens/access-entra-role-assignments.png "Choose gateway-wide access, or select specific model aliases and MCP servers and apply one compatible role.")

### Select identities

On **Select identities**, set **Assign access to** to **User, group, or service principal**, search for your
own account by name, and choose **Select**. In production, prefer an Entra group so membership controls
access. To grant an app running in Azure, set **Assign access to** to **Managed identity** and pick it by
subscription and resource type. You can also enter a principal object ID directly. Select **Next**.

### Review and assign

On **Review + assign**, confirm the role, identities, and scopes, then select **Assign**.

> **Checkpoint**
> Your account appears in **Access** › **Entra ID** with the **AI Gateway Models User** role on the gateway.

<!-- track: cli | Azure CLI -->

### Create the role assignment

`az role assignment create` needs the principal's object ID, the role ID, and the full scope:

```bash title="Bash"
# Give yourself the AI Gateway Models User role (a6b68e3d-…) on the whole gateway, so that you can call its models
az role assignment create \
  --assignee-object-id "$MY_OBJECT_ID" \
  --assignee-principal-type User \
  --role "a6b68e3d-a1f0-4c60-8678-237c050cf4ea" \
  --scope "$GATEWAY_ID" --output none &&
  echo "🛡️ You have the AI Gateway Models User role on $GATEWAY"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
# Give yourself the AI Gateway Models User role (a6b68e3d-…) on the whole gateway, so that you can call its models
az role assignment create `
  --assignee-object-id $MY_OBJECT_ID `
  --assignee-principal-type User `
  --role "a6b68e3d-a1f0-4c60-8678-237c050cf4ea" `
  --scope $GATEWAY_ID --output none
if ($?) { Write-Host "🛡️ You have the AI Gateway Models User role on $GATEWAY" }
```

### Use the helper for other roles and scopes

The lab's helper script maps `user`, `models`, and `tools` to the role IDs, builds the scope for the gateway,
a model alias, or an MCP server, and defaults to the signed-in user:

```bash title="Bash"
# Give yourself the AI Gateway Models User role on the whole gateway
./infra/assign-roles.sh models &&
  echo "🛡️ You have the AI Gateway Models User role on $GATEWAY"

# Or grant the same role on one model alias only, so that calls to other aliases return 403
./infra/assign-roles.sh models "alias:$AI_GATEWAY_MODEL" &&
  echo "🛡️ You have the AI Gateway Models User role on the alias $AI_GATEWAY_MODEL"

# Or grant AI Gateway Tools User on one MCP server, which lets you list and call its tools, but not models
./infra/assign-roles.sh tools "mcp:<mcp-server-name>" &&
  echo "🛡️ You have the AI Gateway Tools User role on the MCP server"

# Or give an Entra group AI Gateway User (models and tools) on the gateway, so that membership controls access
./infra/assign-roles.sh user gateway <group-object-id> Group &&
  echo "🛡️ The group has the AI Gateway User role on $GATEWAY"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
# Give yourself the AI Gateway Models User role on the whole gateway
./infra/assign-roles.ps1 -Role models
if ($?) { Write-Host "🛡️ You have the AI Gateway Models User role on $GATEWAY" }

# Or grant the same role on one model alias only, so that calls to other aliases return 403
./infra/assign-roles.ps1 -Role models -Scope "alias:$env:AI_GATEWAY_MODEL"
if ($?) { Write-Host "🛡️ You have the AI Gateway Models User role on the alias $env:AI_GATEWAY_MODEL" }

# Or grant AI Gateway Tools User on one MCP server, which lets you list and call its tools, but not models
./infra/assign-roles.ps1 -Role tools -Scope "mcp:<mcp-server-name>"
if ($?) { Write-Host "🛡️ You have the AI Gateway Tools User role on the MCP server" }

# Or give an Entra group AI Gateway User (models and tools) on the gateway, so that membership controls access
./infra/assign-roles.ps1 -Role user -PrincipalId <group-object-id> -PrincipalType Group
if ($?) { Write-Host "🛡️ The group has the AI Gateway User role on $GATEWAY" }
```

On GitHub, open [assign-roles.sh](infra/assign-roles.sh) or [assign-roles.ps1](infra/assign-roles.ps1).

For a managed identity, pass its **principal** (object) ID with the type `ServicePrincipal`, for example
from `az identity show -g <resource-group> -n <identity-name> --query principalId -o tsv`.

### Confirm the assignment


> **Checkpoint**

### Choose what to declare

The template grants one AI Gateway role to one principal at the gateway, a model alias, or an MCP server. It

### Change the role or the scope

The parameters come from azd environment values, with the defaults in `infra/main.parameters.json`.
`DATA_PLANE_ROLE` picks the role (`user`, `models`, or `tools`), and `DATA_PLANE_ROLE_SCOPE` picks where to grant
it (`gateway`, or `alias` for the default alias only). To grant only the alias, set the scope and provision again:

```bash title="Bash"
# Grant the role on the default alias instead of the whole gateway
azd env set DATA_PLANE_ROLE_SCOPE alias &&
  echo "📝 DATA_PLANE_ROLE_SCOPE is alias"

# Deploy the templates again, which adds the role assignment on the alias
azd provision &&
  echo "🛡️ You also have the role on the alias $AI_GATEWAY_MODEL"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
# Grant the role on the default alias instead of the whole gateway
azd env set DATA_PLANE_ROLE_SCOPE alias
if ($?) { Write-Host "📝 DATA_PLANE_ROLE_SCOPE is alias" }

# Deploy the templates again, which adds the role assignment on the alias
azd provision
if ($?) { Write-Host "🛡️ You also have the role on the alias $env:AI_GATEWAY_MODEL" }
```

A Bicep deployment only adds or updates resources, so you now hold the role on the gateway **and** on the alias.
To test the narrower scope, remove the gateway-wide assignment with the command in **Remove the role and try
again** under **Verify**: calls to the alias still return `200`. Set `DATA_PLANE_ROLE_SCOPE` back to `gateway` and
run `azd provision` before **Verify**, which re-creates the gateway-wide assignment. For an MCP server, deploy
`infra/role-assignment.bicep` on its own with `role=tools scope=mcp scopeName=<mcp-server-name>`.

## Call the gateway with a token

<!-- track: portal | Portal -->

### Open the playground with Entra ID

Select **Catalog** and pick your model. In the playground toolbar, the **Authentication** list has a
**Token** group with **Microsoft Entra ID** ("Use your signed-in identity.") and an **API key** group with
your runtime keys. When your role allows invoking the model, the portal selects **Microsoft Entra ID** for you.
It checks your permissions through the control plane, so you also need `Microsoft.Authorization/permissions/read`
on the gateway, which **Reader** and higher roles include.

If **Microsoft Entra ID** is disabled, the tooltip tells you to grant access under **Access** › **Entra ID**.
Wait for the role to apply and refresh the page.

### Send a prompt

With **Microsoft Entra ID** selected, send `In one sentence, why use Microsoft Entra ID instead of API keys?`.
The playground's code examples follow the authentication method you select.

> **Checkpoint**
> The model answers, and the **Authentication** list shows **Microsoft Entra ID**, not a key name.

<!-- track: cli | Azure CLI -->

### Get a token

The Azure CLI can issue a token for the AI Gateway audience with your sign-in:

```bash title="Bash"
# Get an access token for the AI Gateway audience, with your Azure CLI sign-in
export AI_GATEWAY_TOKEN="$(az account get-access-token \
  --resource https://azure-api.net/aigateway --query accessToken -o tsv)"
echo "🪪 Token acquired: in AI_GATEWAY_TOKEN (${#AI_GATEWAY_TOKEN} characters, not shown)"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
# Get an access token for the AI Gateway audience, with your Azure CLI sign-in
$env:AI_GATEWAY_TOKEN = az account get-access-token `
  --resource https://azure-api.net/aigateway --query accessToken -o tsv
Write-Host "🪪 Token acquired: in AI_GATEWAY_TOKEN ($($env:AI_GATEWAY_TOKEN.Length) characters, not shown)"
```

Access tokens are short-lived, typically about an hour. Run the command again when you get a `401`.

### Look inside the token

Decode the token's payload (the middle segment) to see what the gateway checks:

```bash title="Bash"
# Decode the token's payload, its middle segment, and show the claims that the gateway checks
echo "🪪 Token claims:"
jq -R 'split(".")[1] | gsub("-";"+") | gsub("_";"/") | @base64d | fromjson
  | {aud, tid, oid, scp, appid}' <<< "$AI_GATEWAY_TOKEN"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
# Take the token's payload, its middle segment, and turn its base64url text into padded base64
$payload = ($env:AI_GATEWAY_TOKEN -split '\.')[1].Replace('-', '+').Replace('_', '/')
$payload = $payload.PadRight($payload.Length + (4 - $payload.Length % 4) % 4, '=')

# Decode the payload, and show the claims that the gateway checks
Write-Host "🪪 Token claims:"
[Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetString([Convert]::FromBase64String($payload)) |
  ConvertFrom-Json | Select-Object aud, tid, oid, scp, appid
```

`aud` is `https://azure-api.net/aigateway`, `scp` includes `Data.All` because the CLI gets a delegated token
for you, and `tid` plus `oid` identify you to per-caller policies.

### Call the model with the bearer token

```bash title="Bash"
# Call the model with your token in the Authorization header, and no api-key header
curl -sS "${AI_GATEWAY_URL%/}/default/models/openai/v1/chat/completions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AI_GATEWAY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"model\":\"$AI_GATEWAY_MODEL\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"Say hello in five words.\"}]}" \
  | jq -r 'if .choices then "🤖 \(.choices[0].message.content)" else "⚠️ \(.error.message // .)" end'
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
# Build the request: the alias in model, and one user message
$body = @{
  model    = $env:AI_GATEWAY_MODEL
  messages = @(@{ role = "user"; content = "Say hello in five words." })
} | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5

# Call the model with your token in the Authorization header, and no api-key header
$response = Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post `
  -Uri "$($env:AI_GATEWAY_URL.TrimEnd('/'))/default/models/openai/v1/chat/completions" `
  -Headers @{ Authorization = "Bearer $env:AI_GATEWAY_TOKEN" } `
  -ContentType "application/json" -Body $body
if ($?) { Write-Host "🤖 $($response.choices[0].message.content)" }
```

> [!WARNING]
> Send a token or a key, never both. A request with an `Authorization` header and an `api-key` header gets `400`.

> **Checkpoint**
> The model replies, and no `api-key` header was sent.

### Review the sample

The only change from an API-key client is where the credential comes from:

```python title="Python"
from azure.identity import DefaultAzureCredential, get_bearer_token_provider
from openai import OpenAI

token_provider = get_bearer_token_provider(
    DefaultAzureCredential(), "https://azure-api.net/aigateway/.default")

client = OpenAI(
    base_url=f"{gateway_url}/default/models/openai/v1",
    api_key=token_provider,   # called before each request, sent as Authorization: Bearer <token>
)
```

```typescript title="TypeScript"
import { DefaultAzureCredential, getBearerTokenProvider } from "@azure/identity";
import OpenAI from "openai";

const getToken = getBearerTokenProvider(
  new DefaultAzureCredential(), "https://azure-api.net/aigateway/.default");

const client = new OpenAI({
  baseURL: `${gatewayUrl}/default/models/openai/v1`,
  apiKey: getToken,   // called before each request, sent as Authorization: Bearer <token>
});
```

```csharp title="C#"
var credential = new DefaultAzureCredential();
AccessToken token = await credential.GetTokenAsync(
    new TokenRequestContext(new[] { "https://azure-api.net/aigateway/.default" }));

request.Headers.Authorization = new AuthenticationHeaderValue("Bearer", token.Token);
```

The OpenAI SDKs for Python (1.106 or later) and TypeScript (5.18 or later) accept a function as the API key.
They call it before each request and send the result as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, and the Azure
Identity token provider refreshes the token before it expires. The C# sample calls the REST endpoint with
`HttpClient` and asks the credential for a token before each call, which also returns a cached token until
it's close to expiry. Don't use an `AzureOpenAI` client here: the gateway exposes the OpenAI v1 API at
`/default/models/openai/v1`.

The complete samples add input checks and print the reply and token usage:

<!-- include: infra/call_with_entra.py -->

<!-- include: infra/call-with-entra.ts -->

<!-- include: infra/CallWithEntra.cs -->

On GitHub, open [call_with_entra.py](infra/call_with_entra.py), [call-with-entra.ts](infra/call-with-entra.ts),
and [CallWithEntra.cs](infra/CallWithEntra.cs) with [CallWithEntra.csproj](infra/CallWithEntra.csproj).

## Verify

Prove that access now follows the role assignment, not a key.

<!-- steps -->

### Confirm the keyless call succeeds

Run the curl call or a code sample from the previous section. It returns `200` with a reply.

### Send a token for the wrong audience

A token for Azure Resource Manager is valid, but not for AI Gateway:

```bash
# Call the model with a token for Azure Resource Manager, the CLI's default audience, and print the status code
echo "🚦 Expect 401 Unauthorized, because the token is for the wrong audience:"
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" "${AI_GATEWAY_URL%/}/default/models/openai/v1/chat/completions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(az account get-access-token --query accessToken -o tsv)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"model\":\"$AI_GATEWAY_MODEL\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"ping\"}]}"
```

The gateway answers `401`: authentication failed, so the role was never checked.

### Remove the role and try again

Remove your assignment, wait a few minutes, get a fresh token, and repeat the curl call:

```bash
# Delete your AI Gateway Models User role assignment (a6b68e3d-…) on the gateway
az role assignment delete --assignee "$MY_OBJECT_ID" \
  --role "a6b68e3d-a1f0-4c60-8678-237c050cf4ea" --scope "$GATEWAY_ID" &&
  echo "🧹 Your AI Gateway Models User role assignment on $GATEWAY is deleted"
```

The gateway now answers `403`: you're authenticated, but no role allows you to invoke the model. In the
playground, the same error offers **Review access**, which opens the role assignments, and
**Copy access request**, which copies your identity, the suggested role, and the scope for an administrator.

### Restore access

Assign the role again (portal, `az role assignment create`, or `./infra/assign-roles.sh models`), wait for it
to apply, and confirm the call returns `200`. On the Bicep + azd track, run `azd provision --no-state`: azd skips
a deployment when the templates and parameters haven't changed, and `--no-state` forces it, so the template
re-creates the assignment.

<!-- /steps -->

> **Checkpoint**
> You called a model with no API key, got `401` for a token with the wrong audience, and `403` while your
> identity had no role.

## Go further

- **Narrow the scope.** Replace the gateway-wide assignment with **AI Gateway Models User** on a single alias
  (`./infra/assign-roles.sh models "alias:<alias>"`). Calls to other aliases now return `403`.
- **Grant tools only.** Give an agent **AI Gateway Tools User** on one MCP server from
  [Federate MCP tools](../04-federate-mcp-tools/README.md), so it can list and call those tools but not
  invoke models.
- **Run without a user.** Deploy the Python sample to an Azure service with a managed identity, assign the
  role to that identity's principal ID, and the same code runs with app-only tokens for the `.default` scope.
  Agent identities work the same way.
- **Budget per person.** Add a cost limit with **Caller identity** as the counter dimension and an override for one Entra identity in
  [Enforce cost budgets](../07-cost-budgets/README.md). Each `tid` and `oid` pair gets its own budget.
- **See who called.** In **Monitoring** › **Settings**, **Token claim attributes** exports claims such as
  `tid`, `oid`, `appid`, and `azp` as `azure.ai_gateway.identity.claims.<claim>` attributes on logs, traces,
  and metrics. See [Monitor usage, cost, and traces](../13-monitoring/README.md).

# Call backends with managed identities

Your platform team runs one gateway per region, and every gateway calls the same Foundry account. Today each
gateway uses its own system-assigned identity, so every new gateway needs a fresh **Foundry User** grant, and
recreating a gateway leaves a stale role assignment behind. The team wants one identity that it owns, grants
once, and attaches to every gateway, with no backend key stored anywhere. In this lab you check the gateway's
system-assigned identity, create a user-assigned identity, give it access to Foundry, and switch a model
provider to it without changing a single client.

![Callers authenticate inbound to the gateway, and the gateway authenticates outbound to each backend](../assets/diagrams/identity-boundaries.svg "Callers authenticate to the gateway with an API key or a Microsoft Entra token. The gateway then calls each backend with its own managed identity, which this lab configures.")

## Before you begin

<!-- setup: tools sign-in extension clone -->

> [!TIP]
> On the **Bicep + azd** track, `azd up` creates its own gateway, model, and key, so you can skip this section. You
> need only the one-time setup above, and permission to create role assignments, for example **Owner** on the
> subscription. To check the system-assigned identity first, run the track in [Create a user-assigned identity and
> give it access](#create-a-user-assigned-identity-and-give-it-access) up to **Read the outputs and the key**, which
> sets the variables, then come back.

- Complete [Publish a Foundry model and make your first call](../02-first-model-call/README.md). You need a
  gateway with a Foundry model provider that uses a managed identity, a model alias, and a runtime API key.
- Every track uses the Azure CLI at least once: the portal can't change the identity of a model provider that already
  exists.
- Permissions:
  - Create a managed identity in the resource group, for example **Contributor** or
    **Managed Identity Contributor**.
  - Attach the identity to the gateway: **Contributor** on the gateway and **Managed Identity Operator** on the
    identity. **Contributor** on a resource group that holds both covers this.
  - Create role assignments on the Foundry account, for example **Owner**, **User Access Administrator**, or
    **Role Based Access Control Administrator**.

Managed identities are free. Nothing in this lab adds charges beyond the model calls you make.

Set these variables once. Every track and the **Verify** section reuse them.

```bash title="Bash"
# Set your gateway, its Foundry provider and Foundry account, and the name of the user-assigned identity to create
export RG="<resource-group>"
export GATEWAY="<gateway>"
export PROVIDER="<provider-name>"                 # the Foundry provider from lab 02, for example foundry-models
export FOUNDRY_RG="<foundry-resource-group>"      # resource group of the Foundry account
export FOUNDRY_ACCOUNT="<foundry-account-name>"   # the account name, not a project or deployment name
export IDENTITY="id-aigateway-backends"           # the user-assigned identity to create
echo "📝 Gateway $GATEWAY in $RG, with provider $PROVIDER and Foundry account $FOUNDRY_ACCOUNT"
echo "🪪 Identity to create: $IDENTITY"

# Read the Foundry account's resource ID and the gateway's runtime URL, and set the alias that you call
export FOUNDRY_ID="$(az cognitiveservices account show -g "$FOUNDRY_RG" -n "$FOUNDRY_ACCOUNT" --query id -o tsv)"
export AI_GATEWAY_URL="https://$(az aigateway show -g "$RG" -n "$GATEWAY" --query properties.frontend.defaultHostname -o tsv)"
export AI_GATEWAY_MODEL="<model-name>"            # the alias you called in lab 02
echo "🆔 Foundry account: $FOUNDRY_ID"
echo "🌐 Runtime URL: $AI_GATEWAY_URL"
echo "🏷️ Model alias: $AI_GATEWAY_MODEL"

# Paste the runtime key from lab 02 without showing it, and don't commit it or write it to a file
read -rsp "AI Gateway API key: " AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY && export AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY && echo
echo "🔑 Key: in AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY (${#AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY} characters, not shown)"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
# Set your gateway, its Foundry provider and Foundry account, and the name of the user-assigned identity to create
$RG              = "<resource-group>"
$GATEWAY         = "<gateway>"
$PROVIDER        = "<provider-name>"              # the Foundry provider from lab 02, for example foundry-models
$FOUNDRY_RG      = "<foundry-resource-group>"     # resource group of the Foundry account
$FOUNDRY_ACCOUNT = "<foundry-account-name>"       # the account name, not a project or deployment name
$IDENTITY        = "id-aigateway-backends"        # the user-assigned identity to create
Write-Host "📝 Gateway $GATEWAY in $RG, with provider $PROVIDER and Foundry account $FOUNDRY_ACCOUNT"
Write-Host "🪪 Identity to create: $IDENTITY"

# Read the Foundry account's resource ID and the gateway's runtime URL, and set the alias that you call
$FOUNDRY_ID = az cognitiveservices account show -g $FOUNDRY_RG -n $FOUNDRY_ACCOUNT --query id -o tsv
$env:AI_GATEWAY_URL = "https://$(az aigateway show -g $RG -n $GATEWAY --query properties.frontend.defaultHostname -o tsv)"
$env:AI_GATEWAY_MODEL = "<model-name>"            # the alias you called in lab 02
Write-Host "🆔 Foundry account: $FOUNDRY_ID"
Write-Host "🌐 Runtime URL: $env:AI_GATEWAY_URL"
Write-Host "🏷️ Model alias: $env:AI_GATEWAY_MODEL"

# Paste the runtime key from lab 02 without showing it, and don't commit it or write it to a file
$env:AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY = Read-Host "AI Gateway API key" -MaskInput
Write-Host "🔑 Key: in AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY ($($env:AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY.Length) characters, not shown)"
```

Don't remember the provider name? List the Foundry providers:
`az aigateway model-provider list -g "$RG" --gateway-name "$GATEWAY" --query "[?properties.kind=='Foundry'].name" -o tsv`.

## How it works

Every call crosses two boundaries. **Inbound**, the caller proves who it is to the gateway with a runtime API key
([lab 10](../10-api-keys/README.md)) or a Microsoft Entra token ([lab 11](../11-entra-rbac/README.md)).
**Outbound**, the gateway proves who *it* is to the backend. The caller never sends a backend credential: you
configure it once on the asset, such as a model provider or an MCP server backend.

For Azure backends, use a managed identity. The gateway requests a Microsoft Entra token for the backend's
audience, `https://cognitiveservices.azure.com/` for Foundry, and Azure RBAC on the backend decides what the
identity can do. For Foundry and Azure OpenAI, grant **Foundry User** on the account. Keep backend API keys for
backends that can't accept an Entra token.

| | System-assigned identity | User-assigned identity | Stored backend key |
|---|---|---|---|
| Created by | Azure, with the gateway. The portal enables it by default. | You, as its own Azure resource | The backend's owner |
| Lifecycle | Tied to the gateway. Deleting the gateway deletes it. | Independent. Attach it to many gateways and keep it when a gateway is recreated. | You store it in the gateway and rotate it |
| Best for | One gateway calling Azure backends | Sharing one identity and its role assignments across gateways | Third-party providers and tools without Entra support |
| Foundry provider setting | `managedIdentity` without `clientId` | `managedIdentity.clientId` set to the identity's client ID | `apiKey` |

Attaching an identity to the gateway doesn't change which identity an asset uses. Each asset names its identity,
so you can move assets one at a time.

## Check the system-assigned identity

Lab 02's provider calls Foundry with the gateway's system-assigned identity. See it before you change anything.

<!-- steps -->

### Look at the identity in the portal

1. Open the [AI Gateway portal](https://ai.gateway.azure.com) and select your gateway.
2. Select **Managed identities**. On **Configure identities**, the **System-assigned identity** card shows
   **Enabled** with a **Principal ID** and a **Tenant ID**.
3. Select **View access**. **Backend access** lists the assets that authenticate with a managed identity. Your
   Foundry provider appears with **System-assigned** as its identity and **Foundry User** as its role.

![The Managed identities page with the system-assigned identity enabled and no user-assigned identities](../assets/screens/managed-identities.png "Configure identities shows the system-assigned identity's principal and tenant IDs, and the user-assigned identities attached to the gateway.")

### Check it with the CLI

```bash title="Bash"
# Show the gateway's identities: the type, and the system-assigned identity's principal and tenant IDs
echo "🪪 Identities of $GATEWAY:"
az aigateway identity show -g "$RG" -n "$GATEWAY" -o json
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
# Show the gateway's identities: the type, and the system-assigned identity's principal and tenant IDs
Write-Host "🪪 Identities of ${GATEWAY}:"
az aigateway identity show -g $RG -n $GATEWAY -o json
```

The output shows `type`, which includes `SystemAssigned`, and the system-assigned `principalId` and `tenantId`.
If the command reports that no identity is assigned to the gateway, enable the system-assigned identity and grant
the new principal **Foundry User** on the Foundry account. `identity assign` returns when the gateway is ready
again:

```bash title="Bash"
# Turn on the gateway's system-assigned identity, and wait until the gateway is ready again
az aigateway identity assign -g "$RG" -n "$GATEWAY" --system-assigned true -o none &&
  echo "🪪 The system-assigned identity of $GATEWAY is on"

# Read the principal ID of the system-assigned identity
PRINCIPAL_ID="$(az aigateway show -g "$RG" -n "$GATEWAY" --query identity.principalId -o tsv)"
echo "🪪 Gateway identity: $PRINCIPAL_ID"

# Give the identity the Foundry User role on the Foundry account, so that the gateway can call its models
az role assignment create --assignee-object-id "$PRINCIPAL_ID" --assignee-principal-type ServicePrincipal \
  --role "53ca6127-db72-4b80-b1b0-d745d6d5456d" --scope "$FOUNDRY_ID" -o none &&
  echo "🛡️ The gateway's identity has the Foundry User role on the Foundry account"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
# Turn on the gateway's system-assigned identity, and wait until the gateway is ready again
az aigateway identity assign -g $RG -n $GATEWAY --system-assigned true -o none
if ($?) { Write-Host "🪪 The system-assigned identity of $GATEWAY is on" }

# Read the principal ID of the system-assigned identity
$PRINCIPAL_ID = az aigateway show -g $RG -n $GATEWAY --query identity.principalId -o tsv
Write-Host "🪪 Gateway identity: $PRINCIPAL_ID"

# Give the identity the Foundry User role on the Foundry account, so that the gateway can call its models
az role assignment create --assignee-object-id $PRINCIPAL_ID --assignee-principal-type ServicePrincipal `
  --role "53ca6127-db72-4b80-b1b0-d745d6d5456d" --scope $FOUNDRY_ID -o none
if ($?) { Write-Host "🛡️ The gateway's identity has the Foundry User role on the Foundry account" }
```

<!-- /steps -->

> [!WARNING]
> Don't turn off the system-assigned identity while assets use it. Disabling it recycles the service principal:
> every backend configured with it fails until you enable it again, and a re-enabled identity gets a new
> principal ID without the old role assignments.

## Create a user-assigned identity and give it access

Pick one track. Each track creates the identity, attaches it to the gateway, and grants it **Foundry User** on
the Foundry account.

<!-- track: portal | Portal -->

### Create and attach the identity

1. In **Managed identities** › **Configure identities**, under **User-assigned identities**, select
   **Add identity**.
2. Select **Create new** and enter the **Name** from `$IDENTITY`, for example `id-aigateway-backends`. The portal
   creates the identity in the gateway's subscription, resource group, and region.
3. Select **Add identity**. The new identity appears in the table with its **Principal** and **Client ID**.

To reuse an identity that already exists, select **Use existing** instead, then pick its **Subscription** and
**User-assigned managed identity**.

### Read the identity's IDs

You need the principal ID to grant access and the client ID to point the provider at the identity.

```bash title="Bash"
# Read the identity's IDs: the resource ID to attach it, the principal ID to grant it access, and the client ID
# to point the provider at it
export IDENTITY_ID="$(az identity show -g "$RG" -n "$IDENTITY" --query id -o tsv)"
export IDENTITY_CLIENT_ID="$(az identity show -g "$RG" -n "$IDENTITY" --query clientId -o tsv)"
export IDENTITY_PRINCIPAL_ID="$(az identity show -g "$RG" -n "$IDENTITY" --query principalId -o tsv)"
echo "🆔 Identity: $IDENTITY_ID"
echo "🪪 Client ID: $IDENTITY_CLIENT_ID"
echo "🪪 Principal ID: $IDENTITY_PRINCIPAL_ID"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
# Read the identity's IDs: the resource ID to attach it, the principal ID to grant it access, and the client ID
# to point the provider at it
$IDENTITY_ID           = az identity show -g $RG -n $IDENTITY --query id -o tsv
$IDENTITY_CLIENT_ID    = az identity show -g $RG -n $IDENTITY --query clientId -o tsv
$IDENTITY_PRINCIPAL_ID = az identity show -g $RG -n $IDENTITY --query principalId -o tsv
Write-Host "🆔 Identity: $IDENTITY_ID"
Write-Host "🪪 Client ID: $IDENTITY_CLIENT_ID"
Write-Host "🪪 Principal ID: $IDENTITY_PRINCIPAL_ID"
```

### Grant Foundry User on the Foundry account

Attaching an identity doesn't grant it any access. In the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com), open the
Foundry account and select **Access control (IAM)** › **Add** › **Add role assignment**. Select **Foundry User**,
assign access to **Managed identity**, select your identity as the member, then select **Review + assign**.

Or grant the role from the command line:

```bash title="Bash"
# Give your identity the Foundry User role on the Foundry account, so that it can call the account's models
az role assignment create --assignee-object-id "$IDENTITY_PRINCIPAL_ID" --assignee-principal-type ServicePrincipal \
  --role "53ca6127-db72-4b80-b1b0-d745d6d5456d" --scope "$FOUNDRY_ID" -o none &&
  echo "🛡️ Identity $IDENTITY has the Foundry User role on the Foundry account"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
# Give your identity the Foundry User role on the Foundry account, so that it can call the account's models
az role assignment create --assignee-object-id $IDENTITY_PRINCIPAL_ID --assignee-principal-type ServicePrincipal `
  --role "53ca6127-db72-4b80-b1b0-d745d6d5456d" --scope $FOUNDRY_ID -o none
if ($?) { Write-Host "🛡️ Identity $IDENTITY has the Foundry User role on the Foundry account" }
```

> **Checkpoint**
> **User-assigned identities** lists your identity, and the Foundry account's **Access control (IAM)** ›
> **Role assignments** shows it with **Foundry User**.

<!-- track: cli | Azure CLI -->

### Create the identity

```bash title="Bash"
# Create the user-assigned identity, in the resource group's region
az identity create -g "$RG" -n "$IDENTITY" -o none &&
  echo "🪪 Identity $IDENTITY is ready"

# Read the identity's IDs: the resource ID to attach it, the principal ID to grant it access, and the client ID
# to point the provider at it
export IDENTITY_ID="$(az identity show -g "$RG" -n "$IDENTITY" --query id -o tsv)"
export IDENTITY_CLIENT_ID="$(az identity show -g "$RG" -n "$IDENTITY" --query clientId -o tsv)"
export IDENTITY_PRINCIPAL_ID="$(az identity show -g "$RG" -n "$IDENTITY" --query principalId -o tsv)"
echo "🆔 Identity: $IDENTITY_ID"
echo "🪪 Client ID: $IDENTITY_CLIENT_ID"
echo "🪪 Principal ID: $IDENTITY_PRINCIPAL_ID"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
# Create the user-assigned identity, in the resource group's region
az identity create -g $RG -n $IDENTITY -o none
if ($?) { Write-Host "🪪 Identity $IDENTITY is ready" }

# Read the identity's IDs: the resource ID to attach it, the principal ID to grant it access, and the client ID
# to point the provider at it
$IDENTITY_ID           = az identity show -g $RG -n $IDENTITY --query id -o tsv
$IDENTITY_CLIENT_ID    = az identity show -g $RG -n $IDENTITY --query clientId -o tsv
$IDENTITY_PRINCIPAL_ID = az identity show -g $RG -n $IDENTITY --query principalId -o tsv
Write-Host "🆔 Identity: $IDENTITY_ID"
Write-Host "🪪 Client ID: $IDENTITY_CLIENT_ID"
Write-Host "🪪 Principal ID: $IDENTITY_PRINCIPAL_ID"
```

The identity is created in the resource group's region. It can live in any resource group or subscription in
the gateway's tenant.

### Attach it to the gateway

`identity assign` adds your identity and keeps the identities the gateway already has, including the
system-assigned one. It returns when the gateway is ready again.

```bash title="Bash"
# Attach your identity to the gateway, keep its other identities, and wait until the gateway is ready again
az aigateway identity assign -g "$RG" -n "$GATEWAY" --user-assigned "$IDENTITY_ID" -o none &&
  echo "🪪 Identity $IDENTITY is attached to $GATEWAY"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
# Attach your identity to the gateway, keep its other identities, and wait until the gateway is ready again
az aigateway identity assign -g $RG -n $GATEWAY --user-assigned $IDENTITY_ID -o none
if ($?) { Write-Host "🪪 Identity $IDENTITY is attached to $GATEWAY" }
```

### Grant Foundry User on the Foundry account

```bash title="Bash"
# Give your identity the Foundry User role on the Foundry account, so that it can call the account's models

  --role "53ca6127-db72-4b80-b1b0-d745d6d5456d" --scope "$FOUNDRY_ID" -o none &&
  echo "🛡️ Identity $IDENTITY has the Foundry User role on the Foundry account"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"

az role assignment create --assignee-object-id $IDENTITY_PRINCIPAL_ID --assignee-principal-type ServicePrincipal `
```

Grant the role on the Foundry account itself, the resource that the provider calls.

> **Checkpoint**

> prints `Foundry User`.

**What you need:** only the one-time setup from **Before you begin**. This track doesn't use your gateway from lab 02:
`azd up` creates a new one, so it works on its own.

### Choose what to declare

The templates declare the identity, its **Foundry User** role on the Foundry account, and the gateway's identities.
A deployment that declares the gateway sets its whole identity block, and the gateway keeps only the identities that
the block lists. That's why the other tracks attach the identity with `az aigateway identity assign`, which keeps the
identities the gateway already has. Here azd owns the gateway, so a template can list both the system-assigned
identity and yours.

The Foundry provider keeps the system-assigned identity for now. You point it at your identity in the next section,
which gives the role assignment time to take effect.

### Review the templates

[resources.bicep](../quickstart/infra/resources.bicep) for the gateway, the Foundry model, its default alias, and the
`app-first-call` key. That provider calls Foundry with the gateway's system-assigned identity. Then `main.bicep` calls
the lab's templates for your identity:

`infra/backend-identity.bicep` creates the user-assigned identity and calls `infra/foundry-user-role.bicep` in the
Foundry account's resource group to grant it **Foundry User**. The account can be in another resource group or
subscription, so you can also deploy this template on its own with `az deployment group create`, passing
`identityName` and `foundryAccountId`:

<!-- include: infra/foundry-user-role.bicep -->

### Read the outputs and the key

Set the variables that the next sections, **Verify**, and **Clean up** use from azd's environment values, and read
the key from the gateway, so that it never shows on screen. The last command lists the user-assigned identities
attached to the gateway.

```bash title="Bash"
# Read the template's outputs: the names, the runtime URL, the alias, and the identity's IDs
export RG="$(azd env get-value AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP)"
export GATEWAY="$(azd env get-value AI_GATEWAY_NAME)"
export PROVIDER="$(azd env get-value AI_GATEWAY_PROVIDER)"
export IDENTITY="$(azd env get-value IDENTITY_NAME)"
export FOUNDRY_ID="$(azd env get-value FOUNDRY_ID)"
export AI_GATEWAY_URL="$(azd env get-value AI_GATEWAY_URL)"
export AI_GATEWAY_MODEL="$(azd env get-value AI_GATEWAY_MODEL)"
export IDENTITY_ID="$(azd env get-value IDENTITY_ID)"
export IDENTITY_CLIENT_ID="$(azd env get-value IDENTITY_CLIENT_ID)"
export IDENTITY_PRINCIPAL_ID="$(azd env get-value IDENTITY_PRINCIPAL_ID)"

# Read the key from the gateway, so that it never lands in a file or a deployment log
export AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY="$(az aigateway api-key list-secrets --ids "$(azd env get-value AI_GATEWAY_ID)/apiKeys/app-first-call" \
  --query primaryKey --output tsv)"
echo "📝 Gateway $GATEWAY in $RG, with provider $PROVIDER and identity $IDENTITY"
echo "🌐 Runtime URL: $AI_GATEWAY_URL"
echo "🏷️ Model alias: $AI_GATEWAY_MODEL"
echo "🪪 Client ID: $IDENTITY_CLIENT_ID"
echo "🔑 Key: in AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY (${#AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY} characters, not shown)"

# List the user-assigned identities attached to the gateway
echo "🪪 User-assigned identities of $GATEWAY:"
az aigateway identity show -g "$RG" -n "$GATEWAY" --query userAssignedIdentities -o json
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
# Read the template's outputs: the names, the runtime URL, the alias, and the identity's IDs
$RG                     = azd env get-value AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP
$GATEWAY                = azd env get-value AI_GATEWAY_NAME

  --query primaryKey --output tsv
Write-Host "📝 Gateway $GATEWAY in $RG, with provider $PROVIDER and identity $IDENTITY"
```

## Point the model provider at the identity

The provider still uses the system-assigned identity. Setting `clientId` in its managed identity settings
switches it to your identity. Clients don't change: they keep calling the same alias with the same key or token.

<!-- track: portal | Portal -->

### Update the provider's authentication

The portal picks the identity only when you import a Foundry account: the **Authentication method** step offers
**Managed identity** with a choice of the system-assigned identity or any attached user-assigned identity, and
grants the selected identity **Foundry User**. To switch a provider that already exists, run these Azure CLI
commands, for example in [Azure Cloud Shell](https://shell.azure.com). They read the provider's `foundry`
settings, set `clientId`, and write the settings back:

```bash title="Bash"
# Read the provider's foundry settings, set clientId to your identity's client ID, and save them in a local file
az aigateway model-provider show -g "$RG" --gateway-name "$GATEWAY" -n "$PROVIDER" --query properties.foundry -o json \
  | jq -c --arg c "$IDENTITY_CLIENT_ID" '.authentication.managedIdentity.clientId=$c' > foundry.json &&
  echo "📄 foundry.json points the provider at client ID $IDENTITY_CLIENT_ID"

# Send the whole foundry object back, show the provider's new authentication settings, and delete the file
echo "🔌 Authentication of $PROVIDER:"
az aigateway model-provider update -g "$RG" --gateway-name "$GATEWAY" -n "$PROVIDER" --foundry @foundry.json \
  --query properties.foundry.authentication
rm foundry.json
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
# Read the provider's foundry settings, set clientId to your identity's client ID, and save them in a local file
$foundry = az aigateway model-provider show -g $RG --gateway-name $GATEWAY -n $PROVIDER --query properties.foundry `
  -o json | ConvertFrom-Json
$foundry.authentication.managedIdentity |
  Add-Member -NotePropertyName clientId -NotePropertyValue $IDENTITY_CLIENT_ID -Force
$foundry | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10 -Compress | Set-Content foundry.json
if ($?) { Write-Host "📄 foundry.json points the provider at client ID $IDENTITY_CLIENT_ID" }

# Send the whole foundry object back, show the provider's new authentication settings, and delete the file
Write-Host "🔌 Authentication of ${PROVIDER}:"
az aigateway model-provider update -g $RG --gateway-name $GATEWAY -n $PROVIDER --foundry "@foundry.json" `
  --query properties.foundry.authentication
Remove-Item foundry.json
```

<!-- track: cli | Azure CLI -->

### Update the provider's authentication

`--foundry` replaces the whole `foundry` object, so a value with only `authentication` fails. Read the current
settings, set `clientId`, and send the whole object back. The endpoint and accounts stay
as they are, and models are separate resources.

```bash title="Bash"
# Read the provider's foundry settings, set clientId to your identity's client ID, and save them in a local file
az aigateway model-provider show -g "$RG" --gateway-name "$GATEWAY" -n "$PROVIDER" --query properties.foundry -o json \
  | jq -c --arg c "$IDENTITY_CLIENT_ID" '.authentication.managedIdentity.clientId=$c' > foundry.json &&
  echo "📄 foundry.json points the provider at client ID $IDENTITY_CLIENT_ID"

# Send the whole foundry object back, show the provider's new authentication settings, and delete the file
echo "🔌 Authentication of $PROVIDER:"
az aigateway model-provider update -g "$RG" --gateway-name "$GATEWAY" -n "$PROVIDER" --foundry @foundry.json \
  --query properties.foundry.authentication
rm foundry.json
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
# Read the provider's foundry settings, set clientId to your identity's client ID, and save them in a local file
$foundry = az aigateway model-provider show -g $RG --gateway-name $GATEWAY -n $PROVIDER --query properties.foundry `
  -o json | ConvertFrom-Json
$foundry.authentication.managedIdentity |
  Add-Member -NotePropertyName clientId -NotePropertyValue $IDENTITY_CLIENT_ID -Force
$foundry | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10 -Compress | Set-Content foundry.json
if ($?) { Write-Host "📄 foundry.json points the provider at client ID $IDENTITY_CLIENT_ID" }

# Send the whole foundry object back, show the provider's new authentication settings, and delete the file

az aigateway model-provider update -g $RG --gateway-name $GATEWAY -n $PROVIDER --foundry "@foundry.json" `
  --query properties.foundry.authentication
Remove-Item foundry.json
```

<!-- track: iac | Bicep + azd -->

### Redeploy the provider with the identity

When `useUserAssignedIdentity` is `true`, `infra/main.bicep` calls [infra/provider.bicep](infra/provider.bicep). It
redeploys the quick start's provider with the same endpoint and account, and adds `clientId` to its managed identity
settings:

```bicep
authentication: {
  kind: 'ManagedIdentity'
  managedIdentity: {
    clientId: identityClientId   // omit clientId to use the system-assigned identity
    resource: 'https://cognitiveservices.azure.com/'
  }
}
```

A deployment replaces the provider's properties, so the template sets all of them, including the display name and
description. Models and aliases are separate resources and aren't touched. You can also deploy
`infra/provider.bicep` on its own to a gateway that lab 02's Bicep track created, with `az deployment group create`,
passing `gatewayName`, `providerName`, `foundryAccountId`, and `identityClientId`. If you created the provider in
the portal or with the CLI, use the **Azure CLI** track's commands instead, which change only the authentication.

<!-- include: infra/provider.bicep -->

azd reads the parameter from `USE_USER_ASSIGNED_IDENTITY`. Set it, provision again, and read the provider's
authentication settings:

```bash title="Bash"
# Tell azd to point the Foundry provider at your identity
azd env set USE_USER_ASSIGNED_IDENTITY true &&
  echo "📝 USE_USER_ASSIGNED_IDENTITY is true"

# Provision again, which now redeploys the provider with infra/provider.bicep
azd provision &&
  echo "🚀 Provider $PROVIDER is redeployed with identity $IDENTITY"

# Show the provider's authentication settings
echo "🔌 Authentication of $PROVIDER:"
az aigateway model-provider show -g "$RG" --gateway-name "$GATEWAY" -n "$PROVIDER" \
  --query properties.foundry.authentication -o json
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
# Tell azd to point the Foundry provider at your identity
azd env set USE_USER_ASSIGNED_IDENTITY true
if ($?) { Write-Host "📝 USE_USER_ASSIGNED_IDENTITY is true" }

# Provision again, which now redeploys the provider with infra/provider.bicep
azd provision
if ($?) { Write-Host "🚀 Provider $PROVIDER is redeployed with identity $IDENTITY" }

# Show the provider's authentication settings
Write-Host "🔌 Authentication of ${PROVIDER}:"
az aigateway model-provider show -g $RG --gateway-name $GATEWAY -n $PROVIDER `
  --query properties.foundry.authentication -o json
```

Each `azd provision` deploys the quick start's gateway and provider first, with the system-assigned identity, then
attaches your identity and points the provider at it again. In between, model calls can fail for a few seconds with
`500`, so don't provision again while the gateway serves real traffic. To switch back, set
`USE_USER_ASSIGNED_IDENTITY` to `false` and run `azd provision`.

<!-- /tracks -->

> **Checkpoint**
> The provider's `authentication` shows `kind: ManagedIdentity` and a `managedIdentity.clientId` equal to
> `$IDENTITY_CLIENT_ID`.

## Verify

<!-- steps -->

### Confirm which identity the provider uses

```bash title="Bash"
# Read the client ID that the provider signs in with, and compare it with your identity's client ID
PROVIDER_CLIENT_ID="$(az aigateway model-provider show -g "$RG" --gateway-name "$GATEWAY" -n "$PROVIDER" \
  --query properties.foundry.authentication.managedIdentity.clientId -o tsv)"
echo "🔌 Provider's client ID: $PROVIDER_CLIENT_ID"
echo "🪪 Identity's client ID: $IDENTITY_CLIENT_ID"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
# Read the client ID that the provider signs in with, and compare it with your identity's client ID
$PROVIDER_CLIENT_ID = az aigateway model-provider show -g $RG --gateway-name $GATEWAY -n $PROVIDER `
  --query properties.foundry.authentication.managedIdentity.clientId -o tsv
Write-Host "🔌 Provider's client ID: $PROVIDER_CLIENT_ID"
Write-Host "🪪 Identity's client ID: $IDENTITY_CLIENT_ID"
```

Both lines print the same client ID. In the portal, **Managed identities** › **View access** now lists your
provider under your identity's name instead of **System-assigned**. The list reflects the configured binding,
not the live role assignment on the Foundry account, so a missing role still shows up only as a failed call.

### Call the model through the gateway

```bash title="Bash"
# Call the alias through the gateway with your runtime key, and print only the HTTP status code
echo "🤖 HTTP status of a call to $AI_GATEWAY_MODEL through the gateway:"
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "HTTP %{http_code}\n" "${AI_GATEWAY_URL%/}/default/models/openai/v1/chat/completions" \
  -H "api-key: $AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"model\":\"$AI_GATEWAY_MODEL\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"ping\"}]}"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
# Build a one-message request for the alias
$body = @{ model = $env:AI_GATEWAY_MODEL; messages = @(@{ role = "user"; content = "ping" }) } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5

# Call the alias through the gateway with your runtime key, and print only the HTTP status code
Write-Host "🤖 HTTP status of a call to $env:AI_GATEWAY_MODEL through the gateway:"
(Invoke-WebRequest -Method Post -Uri "$($env:AI_GATEWAY_URL.TrimEnd('/'))/default/models/openai/v1/chat/completions" `
  -Headers @{ "api-key" = $env:AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY } -ContentType "application/json" -Body $body -SkipHttpErrorCheck).StatusCode
```

Expect `HTTP 200`. A `403` that mentions permissions on the Foundry account means the role assignment hasn't
propagated yet: wait a few minutes and retry.

You called the same alias with the same key as in lab 02. Only the gateway's outbound credential changed, and no
backend key was stored or sent.

<!-- /steps -->

> **Checkpoint**
> The provider names your user-assigned identity, **View access** shows the new binding, and the model still
> answers with `200`.

## Go further

### Use stored credentials when a backend can't take a managed identity

Managed identity needs a backend that accepts Microsoft Entra tokens. When it doesn't, store the backend's own
credential in the gateway, never in the calling app.

| Backend | How the gateway authenticates |
|---|---|
| Microsoft Foundry and Azure OpenAI | **Managed identity** (recommended) or **API key**, chosen in the import's **Authentication method** step |
| OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and other custom models | The provider's API key, entered when you add the custom model ([lab 03](../03-multi-provider-aliases/README.md)) |
| MCP server backends | **None**, **API key**, **OAuth 2.0**, or **Managed identity**, set per backend ([lab 04](../04-federate-mcp-tools/README.md)) |

- Prefer managed identity whenever the backend supports it.
- The gateway stores backend keys and tokens with the asset or connection and never returns them to clients.
- Rotate backend credentials on their own schedule. They're independent of the runtime keys callers use.

### Drop access the system identity no longer needs

After every asset that calls the Foundry account uses the user-assigned identity, the system-assigned identity's
**Foundry User** assignment on that account is unused. Check **View access** › **Backend access** first: remove
the assignment only if no other asset lists **System-assigned** for that account, because later labs in this
series use it. A call that still returns `200` a few minutes after you remove it also proves that the provider
uses the user-assigned identity.

## Clean up

Pick the track you followed.

<!-- track: cli | Portal and Azure CLI -->

Keep the system-assigned identity and its **Foundry User** role. Later labs use them. Remove the user-assigned
identity in this order, so the provider never points at an identity it can't use.

### Switch the provider back to the system-assigned identity

Removing `clientId` selects the system-assigned identity again. As before, read the `foundry` settings, change
them, and write them back:

```bash title="Bash"
# Read the provider's foundry settings, remove clientId, and save them in a local file
az aigateway model-provider show -g "$RG" --gateway-name "$GATEWAY" -n "$PROVIDER" --query properties.foundry -o json \
  | jq -c 'del(.authentication.managedIdentity.clientId)' > foundry.json &&
  echo "📄 foundry.json points the provider at the system-assigned identity"

# Send the whole foundry object back, show the provider's new authentication settings, and delete the file
echo "🔌 Authentication of $PROVIDER:"
az aigateway model-provider update -g "$RG" --gateway-name "$GATEWAY" -n "$PROVIDER" --foundry @foundry.json \
  --query properties.foundry.authentication
rm foundry.json
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
# Read the provider's foundry settings, remove clientId, and save them in a local file
$foundry = az aigateway model-provider show -g $RG --gateway-name $GATEWAY -n $PROVIDER --query properties.foundry `
  -o json | ConvertFrom-Json
$foundry.authentication.managedIdentity.PSObject.Properties.Remove('clientId')
$foundry | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10 -Compress | Set-Content foundry.json
if ($?) { Write-Host "📄 foundry.json points the provider at the system-assigned identity" }

# Send the whole foundry object back, show the provider's new authentication settings, and delete the file
Write-Host "🔌 Authentication of ${PROVIDER}:"
az aigateway model-provider update -g $RG --gateway-name $GATEWAY -n $PROVIDER --foundry "@foundry.json" `
  --query properties.foundry.authentication
Remove-Item foundry.json
```

The output no longer shows `clientId`.

### Detach the identity from the gateway

Remove your identity from the gateway. `identity remove` returns when the gateway is ready again:

```bash title="Bash"
# Detach your identity from the gateway, and wait until the gateway is ready again
az aigateway identity remove -g "$RG" -n "$GATEWAY" --user-assigned "$IDENTITY_ID" -o none &&
  echo "🧹 Identity $IDENTITY is detached from $GATEWAY"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
# Detach your identity from the gateway, and wait until the gateway is ready again
az aigateway identity remove -g $RG -n $GATEWAY --user-assigned $IDENTITY_ID -o none
if ($?) { Write-Host "🧹 Identity $IDENTITY is detached from $GATEWAY" }
```

This detaches only your identity. The system-assigned identity and any other user-assigned identities stay
attached.

In the portal, select the identity in **User-assigned identities**, select the delete button in the toolbar, then
**Detach**. Detaching removes the identity from this gateway only.

### Remove the role assignment and delete the identity

```bash title="Bash"
# Remove your identity's Foundry User role assignment from the Foundry account
az role assignment delete --assignee "$IDENTITY_PRINCIPAL_ID" --role "53ca6127-db72-4b80-b1b0-d745d6d5456d" --scope "$FOUNDRY_ID" &&
  echo "🧹 The Foundry User role assignment of $IDENTITY is deleted"

# Delete the identity, now that nothing uses it
az identity delete -g "$RG" -n "$IDENTITY" &&
  echo "🧹 Identity $IDENTITY is deleted"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
# Remove your identity's Foundry User role assignment from the Foundry account
az role assignment delete --assignee $IDENTITY_PRINCIPAL_ID --role "53ca6127-db72-4b80-b1b0-d745d6d5456d" --scope $FOUNDRY_ID
if ($?) { Write-Host "🧹 The Foundry User role assignment of $IDENTITY is deleted" }

# Delete the identity, now that nothing uses it
az identity delete -g $RG -n $IDENTITY
if ($?) { Write-Host "🧹 Identity $IDENTITY is deleted" }
```

Delete the role assignment first. Deleting the identity alone leaves an orphaned assignment on the account.

> **Checkpoint**
> The model call from **Verify** still returns `200`, and **View access** shows the provider under
> **System-assigned** again.

<!-- track: iac | Bicep + azd -->

### Delete everything azd created

In the `ai-gateway/labs/12-backend-identity` folder, delete the resource group with the gateway, the Foundry account,
and the identity with its role assignment. [`--purge`](../SETUP.md#delete-what-azd-created) also purges the
soft-deleted Foundry account. It takes about ten minutes.

```bash
# Delete everything that azd up created, and purge the Foundry account
azd down --purge --force &&
  echo "🧹 Everything that azd up created is deleted"
```

<!-- /tracks -->

`azd down` doesn't touch your gateway from lab 02 or its system-assigned identity, because the Bicep + azd track
created its own gateway.

# Monitor usage, cost, and traces

Your gateway now serves several apps. Finance asks what the models cost per team, an app owner reports
intermittent failures, and nobody can tell whether a policy or the backend rejected those calls. In this lab you
send the gateway's OpenTelemetry signals to Application Insights and answer all three questions from the built-in
**Monitoring** dashboard, down to a single request's trace.

![AI Gateway exports metrics, logs, and traces to Application Insights or any OTLP endpoint](../assets/diagrams/observability.svg "The gateway exports each telemetry signal over OTLP. With Application Insights, the Monitoring page reads the same data back as a dashboard.")

<!-- widget: request-lifecycle -->

## Before you begin

<!-- setup: tools sign-in extension clone -->

> [!TIP]
> On the **Bicep + azd** track, `azd up` creates its own gateway, model, key, and Application Insights, so you can
> skip this section. You need only the one-time setup above, and permission to create role assignments, for example
> **Owner** on the subscription.

- Complete [Publish a Foundry model and make your first call](../02-first-model-call/README.md). You need a gateway,
  an imported model, a callable alias, and a runtime API key from **Access** › **Keys**.
- Permission to change the gateway, for example **Contributor** on its resource group, **and** permission to
  create role assignments, for example **Owner** or **Role Based Access Control Administrator**. Setup grants the
  gateway's managed identity a role on the telemetry destination. To reuse an existing Application Insights
  resource, you also need **Application Insights Contributor** on it.
- Run the scripts and samples from the lab's folder, `~/ai-gateway/labs/13-monitoring`.

Set these variables once. The tracks and the traffic script reuse them.

```bash title="Bash"
# Name your gateway from lab 02, and the alias that the traffic script calls
export RG="<resource-group>"
export GATEWAY="<gateway>"
export AI_GATEWAY_MODEL="<model-name>"     # a callable alias, for example the one you used in lab 02

export WS="https://management.azure.com$GATEWAY_ID/workspaces/default"

echo "🆔 Gateway ID: $GATEWAY_ID"
echo "🌐 Runtime URL: $AI_GATEWAY_URL"

# Paste the runtime key you created in Access › Keys, without showing it: don't commit it or write it to a file
read -rsp "AI Gateway API key: " AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY && export AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY && echo
echo "🔑 Key: in AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY (${#AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY} characters, not shown)"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
# Name your gateway from lab 02, and the alias that the traffic script calls
```

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Did you configure monitoring before the 2026-08-28 release? Reconfigure it to get logs, traces, cost metrics, and
> policy spans: on the **Monitoring** page select **Settings**, disable monitoring, and configure it again. You can
> select the same Application Insights resource.

## How it works

The gateway emits three OpenTelemetry signals and exports each one **independently** over OTLP, to Azure Application
Insights or to any OTLP endpoint (for example Datadog, Splunk, Grafana Cloud, or your own collector). Configure only
the signals you need. Telemetry follows the OpenTelemetry GenAI and MCP semantic conventions, such as
`gen_ai.request.model`, `gen_ai.operation.name`, and `mcp.method.name`, and adds gateway attributes such as the API
key, alias, resolved model, and policy type.

When the destination is Application Insights and all three signals are on, the **Monitoring** page turns that data
into a dashboard. Estimated cost is **observed tokens × public pricing**: use it to spot trends and compare callers,
then reconcile with provider billing or Azure Cost Management for financial reporting.

| Signal | What the gateway sends | Where it lands with Application Insights | Dashboard uses it for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Metrics | Token usage and estimated token cost, by model, token type, API key, and caller | Azure Monitor workspace (managed Prometheus) linked to Application Insights | Tokens and **Estimated model cost** |
| Traces | One root span per request, with child spans for each stage and each policy that ran | `OTelSpans` table in the Log Analytics workspace | Calls, outcomes, blocked traces, the trace waterfall |
| Logs | Request records with status, caller, model, and the token usage the backend reported | `OTelLogs` table in the Log Analytics workspace | Correlated logs and caller attribution |

## Connect Application Insights

Pick one track. Both end with the gateway exporting all three signals to an Application Insights resource named
`<gateway>-insights`.

<!-- track: portal | Portal -->

### Start the setup

Open the [AI Gateway portal](https://ai.gateway.azure.com) and select your gateway from the gateway switcher. Select
**Monitoring**. If monitoring isn't configured yet, the page shows **Set up monitoring**. Select
**Configure telemetry**. The wizard has three steps: **Destination**, **Authentication**, and **Review and apply**.

### Choose a destination

On **Destination**, select **New Azure Application Insights resource** and keep the suggested name,
`<gateway>-insights`. Select **Next**.

> [!TIP]
> The other choices are **Existing Azure Application Insights resource**, for a component you already have, and
> **Custom OpenTelemetry destination**, which takes separate **Metrics endpoint**, **Logs endpoint**, and
> **Traces endpoint** URLs. Leave an endpoint empty to turn that signal off. The built-in dashboard only reads
> Application Insights, so with a custom destination you use your own platform's views.

### Review authentication

On **Authentication**, the gateway exports with its managed identity. If none is enabled, the wizard enables the
system-assigned identity for you. It also assigns the **Monitoring Metrics Publisher** role on the destination's
Data Collection Rule when you apply.

Leave **Include recommended token claims in telemetry** selected. It adds Microsoft Entra caller claims to the
telemetry, which [Attribute tokens and cost with OpenTelemetry](../14-otel-chargeback/README.md) builds on. Select
**Next**.

### Apply the configuration

On **Review and apply**, select **Apply**. The wizard shows each step as it runs: **Register resource providers**,
**Resolve managed identity**, **Provision destination**, **Discover OTLP endpoints**,
**Assign Monitoring Metrics Publisher role**, and **Create telemetry exporter**. If a step fails, fix the cause
shown in the message and select **Retry**. If an Azure Policy assignment blocks a step, check the Activity Log for
the denied operation.

> **Checkpoint**
> The **Monitoring** page shows the **Overview**, **Models**, **Tools**, **Policies**, and **Traces** tabs, with
> **Open in Azure portal** and **Settings** in the header.

<!-- track: iac | Bicep + azd -->

**What you need:** only the one-time setup from **Before you begin**. This track doesn't use your gateway from lab 02:
`azd up` creates a new one, so it works on its own.

### Choose what to declare

The templates declare what the portal's wizard sets up: a Log Analytics workspace, a workspace-based Application
Insights component with OTLP ingestion turned on, and a gateway telemetry exporter of kind `OpenTelemetry` that
sends metrics, logs, and traces to the component's OTLP endpoints with the recommended token claims. When OTLP
ingestion turns on, Azure creates a managed resource group, `ai_<component>_<id>_managed`, with the Data Collection
Rule and the Azure Monitor workspace for the metrics. The template reads the endpoints back from the component.

The gateway's managed identity also needs **Monitoring Metrics Publisher** on that Data Collection Rule. Azure locks
the managed resource group with a deny assignment that blocks deployments, so Bicep can't assign the role there.
Instead, `azure.yaml` assigns it with the Azure CLI in a `postprovision` hook, which azd runs after each deployment.

The sample's exporter kind, `applicationInsights`, is legacy: the portal flags it because it no longer activates the
OTLP signals the dashboard needs. `infra/monitoring.bicep` keeps it for reference, switched off by
`deployLegacyExporter`.

### Review the templates

`infra/main.bicep` creates the resource group `rg-<environment name>` and calls the quick start's
[resources.bicep](../quickstart/infra/resources.bicep) for the gateway, the Foundry model, its default alias, and the
`app-first-call` key. Then it calls `infra/monitoring.bicep` for the destination and `infra/otel-exporter.bicep` to
connect the gateway to it:

<!-- include: infra/main.bicep -->

`infra/monitoring.bicep` creates the Log Analytics workspace and the Application Insights component, and turns on
OTLP ingestion when `enableOtlpIngestion` is `true`. You can also deploy it on its own to your gateway's resource
group with `az deployment group create`, then connect it in the portal with **Existing Azure Application Insights
resource**:

<!-- include: infra/monitoring.bicep -->

`infra/otel-exporter.bicep` creates the exporter. The `claimAttributes` parameter lists the token claims to add to
the telemetry, and the signals that carry each one. Its default matches **Include recommended token claims in
telemetry**:

<!-- include: infra/otel-exporter.bicep -->

`azure.yaml` holds the `postprovision` hook that grants the role:

### Deploy with azd up

Move into the lab's folder, create an azd environment named `aigw-lab13` in your current subscription, then provision
everything. It takes about four minutes.

```bash title="Bash"
# Move into the lab's folder, which holds the azd project
cd ~/ai-gateway/labs/13-monitoring &&
  echo "📂 Lab folder: $(pwd)"

# Create an azd environment in your current subscription, so that azd doesn't prompt you
azd env new aigw-lab13 --location eastus2 --subscription "$(az account show --query id --output tsv)" &&
  echo "📝 azd environment aigw-lab13 deploys to eastus2"

# Provision the gateway, its model, alias, and key, and Application Insights, and connect the gateway to it
azd up &&
  echo "🚀 Gateway deployed: $(azd env get-value AI_GATEWAY_URL)"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
# Move into the lab's folder, which holds the azd project
Set-Location ~/ai-gateway/labs/13-monitoring
if ($?) { Write-Host "📂 Lab folder: $(Get-Location)" }

# Create an azd environment in your current subscription, so that azd doesn't prompt you
azd env new aigw-lab13 --location eastus2 --subscription (az account show --query id --output tsv)
if ($?) { Write-Host "📝 azd environment aigw-lab13 deploys to eastus2" }

# Provision the gateway, its model, alias, and key, and Application Insights, and connect the gateway to it

```

For another region, pick one where AI Gateway and the `gpt-6-luna` model are available, as in [Find the available

### Read the outputs and the key

Set the variables that the next sections and **Verify** use from azd's environment values, and read the key from
the gateway, so that it never shows on screen. The last command lists the gateway's telemetry exporters.

```bash title="Bash"
# Read the gateway's names, URLs, and alias, and the Log Analytics workspace ID, from azd's environment values
export RG="$(azd env get-value AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP)"
export GATEWAY="$(azd env get-value AI_GATEWAY_NAME)"
export AI_GATEWAY_MODEL="$(azd env get-value AI_GATEWAY_MODEL)"
export API="api-version=2025-09-01-preview"
export GATEWAY_ID="$(azd env get-value AI_GATEWAY_ID)"
export WS="https://management.azure.com$GATEWAY_ID/workspaces/default"
export AI_GATEWAY_URL="$(azd env get-value AI_GATEWAY_URL)"
export LAW_CUSTOMER_ID="$(azd env get-value LOG_ANALYTICS_CUSTOMER_ID)"
echo "📝 Gateway $GATEWAY in $RG"
echo "🌐 Runtime URL: $AI_GATEWAY_URL"
echo "🏷️ Model alias: $AI_GATEWAY_MODEL"
echo "🆔 Log Analytics workspace ID: $LAW_CUSTOMER_ID"

# Read the key from the gateway, so that it never shows on screen or lands in a file
export AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY="$(az aigateway api-key list-secrets --ids "$GATEWAY_ID/apiKeys/app-first-call" \
  --query primaryKey --output tsv)"
echo "🔑 Key: in AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY (${#AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY} characters, not shown)"

# List the gateway's telemetry exporters with az rest, because the aigateway extension doesn't manage them yet
echo "📊 Telemetry exporters on $GATEWAY:"
az rest --url "$WS/telemetryExporters?$API" --query "value[].{name:name, kind:properties.kind}" -o table
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
# Read the gateway's names, URLs, and alias, and the Log Analytics workspace ID, from azd's environment values
$RG                     = azd env get-value AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP
$GATEWAY                = azd env get-value AI_GATEWAY_NAME
$env:AI_GATEWAY_MODEL   = azd env get-value AI_GATEWAY_MODEL
$API                    = "api-version=2025-09-01-preview"
$GATEWAY_ID             = azd env get-value AI_GATEWAY_ID

$env:AI_GATEWAY_URL     = azd env get-value AI_GATEWAY_URL
$LAW_CUSTOMER_ID        = azd env get-value LOG_ANALYTICS_CUSTOMER_ID
Write-Host "📝 Gateway $GATEWAY in $RG"
Write-Host "🌐 Runtime URL: $env:AI_GATEWAY_URL"
Write-Host "🏷️ Model alias: $env:AI_GATEWAY_MODEL"
Write-Host "🆔 Log Analytics workspace ID: $LAW_CUSTOMER_ID"

# Read the key from the gateway, so that it never shows on screen or lands in a file
$env:AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY = az aigateway api-key list-secrets --ids "$GATEWAY_ID/apiKeys/app-first-call" `
  --query primaryKey --output tsv
Write-Host "🔑 Key: in AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY ($($env:AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY.Length) characters, not shown)"

# List the gateway's telemetry exporters with az rest, because the aigateway extension doesn't manage them yet
```

on each, then one request for an alias that doesn't exist, so you also get a failure to investigate.

```bash title="Bash"
# Send ten chat completions, each with an x-correlation-id header, then one call to an alias that doesn't exist
```

## Tour the dashboard

Each tab answers a different question. Use the time range buttons (**1H**, **24H**, **7D**, **30D**) to match your
traffic.

<!-- steps -->

### Overview: is the gateway healthy, and what does it cost?

Select **Monitoring** › **Overview**. The cards summarize the range: **Estimated model cost**, **Model calls**,
**Tool calls**, **Trace failure rate**, and **Blocked traces**. Below them, **Model and tool calls over time**
stacks both kinds of traffic, **Top models** ranks models by estimated cost with their 4xx and 5xx error rates, and
**Top tool servers** ranks MCP servers by calls. **Recent traces requiring attention** and
**Top blocking policies** take you straight to problems.

![The Monitoring overview with estimated cost, calls, failure rate, and top models](../assets/screens/monitoring-overview.png "Overview: estimated model cost, model and tool calls, failure rate, blocked traces, and the top models and tool servers.")

### Models: who uses which model, and how many tokens?

Select **Models**. Each row is a responding model with its **Aliases**, **Calls**, **Input tokens**,
**Output tokens**, **Cached input tokens**, **Token share**, error counts, **Caller identities**, and
**Estimated cost**. **Model usage by caller identity** breaks usage and estimated cost down by API key or Entra
caller. That's your first view of cost by API key and model.

> [!NOTE]
> If you see "Model token and estimated cost data are incomplete until you add a Prometheus access token", follow
> the prompt: run `az account get-access-token --resource https://prometheus.monitor.azure.com --query accessToken -o tsv`
> and paste the value into **Prometheus access token**.

### Tools: which MCP tools are called?

Select **Tools**. You see **Total tool calls**, **Active tool servers**, **Usage by tool server**,
**Top tools within tool servers**, and **Tool usage by caller identity**. It stays empty until agents call tools
through the gateway, as in [Federate MCP tools behind one endpoint](../04-federate-mcp-tools/README.md).

### Policies: what did governance block?

Select **Policies**. The summary shows **Requests blocked**, **Caller identities blocked**, and
**Assets with blocked calls**. The table lists each **Policy type** with **Allowed requests**,
**Blocked requests**, and **Last executed**. After [Throttle tokens per caller](../06-token-limits/README.md), the
token limit's `429` responses show up here.

### Traces: find the failed request

Select **Traces**. Each row shows **Time**, **Assets**, **Outcome**, and **Applied policies**. Find the request
for `does-not-exist` from the script, or use **Search trace ID, asset, policy, or reason**.

<!-- /steps -->

> **Checkpoint**
> **Overview** shows the model calls you sent and a non-zero **Estimated model cost**, **Models** shows your API key
> as a caller identity, and **Traces** lists the failed request.

## Follow a request through the trace waterfall

A gateway-aware trace shows where time went and which policies ran, so you can tell a policy rejection from a
backend failure at a glance.

<!-- steps -->

### Open a successful trace

On **Traces**, select a successful model call. The header shows the **Trace ID**, the number of **Spans**, and the
**Duration**.

### Read the waterfall

**Trace waterfall** draws parent-first spans on one timeline. The root span is the model request, for example
`Model · <model-name>` on `POST /default/models/*`. Under it:

| Child span | What it measures |
|---|---|
| **inbound** | Work before the backend call. Each policy that ran is a child span, such as `policy costLimit` with its configuration. |
| **backend** | The call to the provider, for example `HTTP POST` on `/openai/v1/chat/completions`. |
| **outbound** | Work on the response before it returns to the client. |
| **response transfer** | Sending the response back to the client. |

![A trace waterfall with inbound, backend, outbound, and response transfer spans and a cost limit policy span](../assets/screens/monitoring-trace.png "The waterfall splits gateway time from backend time, and each policy that ran appears as its own span.")

### Read the correlated logs

Under **Correlated logs**, expand the request log and switch between **Code** and **Tree**. Look for:

- `gen_ai.operation.name` (for example `chat`), `gen_ai.request.model` (the alias you sent), and
  `gen_ai.response.model` (the versioned model that answered).
- `azure.ai_gateway.client.usage.prompt_tokens`, `...completion_tokens`, and `...total_tokens`: the usage the
  backend reported for this one call.

<!-- /steps -->

> **Checkpoint**
> You can point to the policy spans under **inbound**, compare **backend** time with total time, and read the
> token usage of one request in its correlated log.

## Query telemetry with KQL

The dashboard reads the `OTelSpans` and `OTelLogs` tables in the Log Analytics workspace behind Application Insights.
You can query them directly to build your own reports and alerts.

<!-- steps -->

### Open Logs

In the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com), open the Log Analytics workspace linked to your Application Insights
resource (`<gateway>-logs` if you used the Bicep + azd track) and select **Logs**. Switch the editor to **KQL mode**.

### Run the starter queries

Copy a query from [infra/queries.kql](infra/queries.kql) and run it. Start with query 2 (calls by alias, resolved
model, and API key) and query 3 (token usage per model and API key).

<!-- include: infra/queries.kql kusto -->

On GitHub, open [infra/queries.kql](infra/queries.kql).

To run a query from the command line instead, pass the workspace's customer ID to
`az monitor log-analytics query`. The command comes from the `log-analytics` extension, which the Azure CLI offers to
install the first time. On the Bicep + azd track, `LAW_CUSTOMER_ID` already holds the ID. Otherwise, set it to the
**Workspace ID** on the workspace's **Overview** page. This short query counts the model calls of the last hour by
alias and status code:

```bash title="Bash"
# Count the model calls of the last hour by alias and status code, from the gateway's spans in Log Analytics
echo "📊 Model calls in the last hour, by alias and status code:"
az monitor log-analytics query -w "$LAW_CUSTOMER_ID" -o table --analytics-query \
  'OTelSpans | where TimeGenerated > ago(1h) | where Kind =~ "Server" and tostring(Attributes["http.route"]) contains "/models/" | summarize Calls = count() by Model = tostring(Attributes["gen_ai.request.model"]), Status = toint(Attributes["http.response.status_code"])'
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
# Count the model calls of the last hour by alias and status code, from the gateway's spans in Log Analytics
Write-Host "📊 Model calls in the last hour, by alias and status code:"
az monitor log-analytics query -w $LAW_CUSTOMER_ID -o table --analytics-query `
  'OTelSpans | where TimeGenerated > ago(1h) | where Kind =~ "Server" and tostring(Attributes["http.route"]) contains "/models/" | summarize Calls = count() by Model = tostring(Attributes["gen_ai.request.model"]), Status = toint(Attributes["http.response.status_code"])'
```

These queries are starting points. Attribute names follow the OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions plus gateway
attributes. Run `OTelSpans | take 10` to see what your data carries, and adapt names before you build alerts on
them.

<!-- /steps -->

> **Checkpoint**
> Query 2 returns one row per alias and API key with your call count, and query 3 returns input and output token
> totals that match the order of magnitude on the **Models** tab.

### Confirm all signals are flowing

Open **Settings**. All three signals point at your Application Insights resource, and the dashboard doesn't show

```powershell title="PowerShell"

```

The exporter that the portal and the Bicep + azd track create has kind `OpenTelemetry`. Kind `applicationInsights` is the legacy exporter
